title: Product Stewardship Amendment (Packaging and Plastics) Bill 2019
short_title: Product Stewardship Amendment (Packaging and Plastics) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create a compulsory stewardship scheme for consumer packaging and certain single-use plastics, imposing recycling targets, product bans and responsibilities on industry.
It would target reusable, recyclable or compostable packaging by 2025, introduce a national 20c beverage container deposit by 2021 and phase in plastic bans.
The scheme would require reports from larger businesses and allow exemptions supplying plastic straws to people with disability where they provide convenience and reduce harm.
changes: Lightweight plastic bags and microbeads would be banned by 1 January 2021.
Specified non-compostable plastic utensils and expanded polystyrene food containers would be banned by 1 January 2023.
Beverage container caps and lids would have to remain attached by 2023.
The Minister could direct scheme members whose progress towards targets is inadequate.
summary.affected: Packaging and plastics manufacturers, importers, distributors, scheme members and consumers using the covered products are affected.
